title: Every app module that defines a table model ships a packaged migration history
intent: A deployed Terp app builds its schema from packaged migrations, never from dev-time schema auto-creation (the production boot guard applies the packaged histories) — so a module that declares a table model but ships no migration revision would deploy with that table missing: the boot guard checks only declared histories, so it never notices, and the first request fails on a nonexistent table. This rule fails the build instead, the build-time complement to the runtime boot guard (the two halves of the migration control). Generate and commit the module's migration revision.
reference: terp migrate make <name> generates the module's migrations/versions/ revision; assert_migrations_current is the production boot guard, create_all the refused dev shortcut.

runtime.rationale: The migration runtime owns the seam but does not yet refuse this rule's core violation: assert_no_homeless_tables fails closed only on an unowned table wired into an owned one by a foreign key (deliberately scoped against fixture false-positives), and the boot guard assert_migrations_current refuses only pending revisions of declared histories. A standalone missing history -- the case this rule exists for -- is visible in the same seam's live metadata but not yet refused, so it is held at build time only.
